details.description: Code Llama 70B is the largest base model in Meta's Code Llama family, released January 29, 2024 as an update to the original 7B/13B/34B lineup from August 2023. Meta trained it on 1 trillion tokens of code and code-related data, double the 500 billion tokens used for the smaller sizes. Like the 34B size, it is a general-purpose foundation checkpoint, distinct from the Python-specialized and instruction-tuned 70B variants released alongside it.
advantages: Scores 53.0% pass@1 on HumanEval and 62.4% pass@1 on MBPP (Code Llama paper, Table 2).
Trained on 1 trillion tokens of code data, twice the 500 billion tokens used for the 7B/13B/34B Code Llama sizes (Meta Code Llama blog).
disadvantages: Unlike the 7B and 13B Code Llama sizes, the 34B and 70B models were not trained with fill-in-the-middle (infilling) capability (Meta Code Llama blog).
Base model without instruction-tuning; Meta's Hugging Face model card positions the separate Code Llama - Instruct 70B variant as safer for code-assistant and chat-style use.

notes: Catalog's max_input/max_output_tokens of 4096 matches Fireworks' own listed ~4.09k-token serving context for this hosted model, which is notably narrower than Meta's Hugging Face model card, describing the 70B base checkpoint as fine-tuned on 16K-token sequences and usable up to 100K tokens at inference (that extended-context claim does not apply to the 70B Instruct sibling, per its own card).
